text: Ravi's payment just failed. Priya, the organizer, didn't chase him. Here's what her treasurer did next.
Priya, a composite organizer, is her circle's bank, collector, and insurer.
Nineteen million US households are underbanked. In Sub-Saharan Africa, over a quarter of adults save in clubs.
Her rules, in Hindi, go in. Turnkeeper compiles them into a frozen charter: pot order, fees, quorum, hash.
Each member sees the fees up front, then approves the schedule once, on PayPal.
Each member holds a signed mandate for their own agent. It's our own AP2-style design, with a server-attested signature.
Three days out, the forecast flags Ravi: late twice, and his last payday was three weeks before the due date. He gets a nudge in Hindi.
Round three runs on its own. Five charges complete, confirmed through the PayPal Agent Toolkit. Ravi's charge is declined, labelled sandbox-injected.
Ravi replies.
शुक्रवार को सैलरी आएगी, तब भर दूंगा।
Salary comes Friday. That becomes a promise with a date.
The agent proposes only what the charter allows: the buffer covers Ravi now, he repays by PayPal invoice, and swaps turns with Tomas.
The members' agents answer inside their mandates. Tomas's accepts an earlier turn; Ravi's asks him first. Five say yes, four are needed, and Priya taps once.
The agent reschedules the board, and sends Ravi an invoice with a QR code.
The ledger checks out, and PayPal Payouts sends Dev the pot, net of fees, with PayPal's own IDs.
A two hundred thirty dollar charge, over the two hundred dollar mandate, is refused before PayPal is called.
Round four is clean: six charges, one payout, and Priya typed nothing.
The model proposes, a policy engine decides, and people and member agents act inside signed mandates.
Vault, Orders, Payouts, Invoicing, Webhooks and Balances, with tools behind MCP. A free model can drive it; this take ran in rules mode.
In a hundred rules-mode runs, ninety-five percent of proposals were charter-legal, and zero illegal actions executed.
And the full story ran live on the PayPal sandbox.
PayPal's money pooling collects for one group purchase. Turnkeeper is the pool that rotates.
It's sandbox only, the buffer is optional, there are no credit claims, and our mandates are AP2-style, not AP2 support.
Turnkeeper. Your circle, kept.
